brief: ARCHITECT-OWNED, PASS 0 — hard deadline: before any kanji packet goes out. The canonical component list (~250 ComponentDef items; exempt from the 150-item cap, V02): id c-<kebab-name>, char, name (lowercase canonical English keyword), variants (亻 for 人, 氵 for 水, …), hint ≤ 80 chars. Must include every name in CONTENT_GUIDE §12.1 plus the primitives the N5–N2 set needs (卜 divination, 罒 net, 尺 ruler, 丶 drop, 亠 lid, 禾 grain, 卩 seal, 殳 weapon, 爪 claw, 玉 jewel, 疒 sickness, 穴 hole, 聿 brush, 臣 retainer, 至 arrive, 臼 mortar, 血 blood, 行 go, 辛 spicy, 非 wrong, 革 leather, 風 wind, 鬼 demon, 鹿 deer, 麦 wheat, 黄 yellow, 黒 black, 歯 tooth, …) and the stroke-type escape hatch (drop, hook, lid, divination, cross, dot). Accompanied by a one-off check in scripts/ that decomposes every one of the 1,000 planned kanji characters (station-allocation §3) into listed names from an offline IDS/KanjiVG-derived table and fails on any character that cannot be decomposed; a kanji that is itself a primitive lists its own name. Writers never edit this file.

ARCHITECT-OWNED, PASS 0 — required by V30 before the first validation run. A JSON array of denied terms (franchise titles, characters, studios, games, mascots, brands, product names, real living people, real company signage), each in Latin and katakana forms, plus a `patterns` array of regexes. Not a ContentFile; exempt from V01–V08 shape rules; `type: "denylist"`.

Hiragana, exactly 104 items in this order (ids k-h-<ime-romaji>, see guide §3): basic 46 → あいうえお かきくけこ さしすせそ たちつてと なにぬねの はひふへほ まみむめも やゆよ らりるれろ わを ん; dakuten 20 → がぎぐげご ざじずぜぞ だぢづでど ばびぶべぼ; handakuten 5 → ぱぴぷぺぽ; yōon 33 → きゃきゅきょ しゃしゅしょ ちゃちゅちょ にゃにゅにょ ひゃひゅひょ みゃみゅみょ りゃりゅりょ ぎゃぎゅぎょ じゃじゅじょ びゃびゅびょ ぴゃぴゅぴょ. Station 1 absorbs basic+dakuten+handakuten (71), Station 2 the yōon (33 = the 11 rows above × 3; the ぢゃ row is deliberately omitted, so the file holds exactly 46 + 20 + 5 + 33 = 104 items). Each item: shape mnemonic ≤ 160 chars (one concrete picture + sound hook, no franchise), exampleWord = a common N5 word written in kana, lookalikes for ね/れ/わ, め/ぬ, さ/き, は/ほ, る/ろ. Row = consonant row; ん row "nn". Katakana is a separate file — do not include.

Katakana, exactly 134 items in this order (ids k-k-<ime-romaji>): basic 46 → アイウエオ カキクケコ サシスセソ タチツテト ナニヌネノ ハヒフヘホ マミムメモ ヤユヨ ラリルレロ ワヲ ン; dakuten 20 → ガギグゲゴ ザジズゼゾ ダヂヅデド バビブベボ; handakuten 5 → パピプペポ; yōon 33 → キャキュキョ シャシュショ チャチュチョ ニャニュニョ ヒャヒュヒョ ミャミュミョ リャリュリョ ギャギュギョ ジャジュジョ ビャビュビョ ピャピュピョ; extended 30 (type "extended", row "ext", id segment in parentheses, display romaji Hepburn) → ファ(fa) フィ(fi) フェ(fe) フォ(fo) フュ(fyu) ヴァ(va) ヴィ(vi) ヴ(vu) ヴェ(ve) ヴォ(vo) ヴュ(vyu) シェ(she) ジェ(je) チェ(che) ツァ(tsa) ツィ(tsi) ツェ(tse) ツォ(tso) ティ(thi) ディ(dhi) テュ(thu) デュ(dhu) トゥ(twu) ドゥ(dwu) ウィ(whi) ウェ(whe) ウォ(who) イェ(ye) クァ(kwa) クォ(kwo). Station 2 absorbs the basic 46; Station 3 the remaining 88 (20 + 5 + 33 + 30; the ヂャ row is deliberately omitted so the file holds exactly 134 items). exampleWord = a common loanword containing the kana (tag-free WordExample). Mnemonics may point to the hiragana twin or the source kanji (カ from 加). lookalikes for シ/ツ, ソ/ン, ク/ケ/タ, コ/ユ, ウ/ワ, ヲ/フ. No franchise names in example words (no brands).

N5 file 1 of 6 — the starter set. Frequency band: the ~150 most frequent beginner words. Content: greetings & set phrases incl. aizuchi (おはようございます, はい, ええ, そうですね, すみません, いただきます … ~25, pos expr/int, tags greetings/aizuchi/set-phrase); pronouns & people/family core (私, あなた, 人, 友達, 先生, 学生, 父, 母, 家族 … ~35); school & study nouns (学校, 教室, 本, ノート, 鉛筆, 宿題, 日本語 … ~20); numbers 一〜十, 百, 千, 万 and basic counters 〜つ 〜人 〜枚 〜本 〜円 〜歳 (pos num/counter, tag numbers/counter, ~25); particles & copula/aux (は が を に で へ と も の か ね よ から まで です ます ません でした — pos prt/aux, functional glosses in parentheses, ~15); question words (何, 誰, どこ, いつ, どれ, どの, どう, いくら, いくつ, なぜ ~10). ORDER MATTERS: items 1–80 are the White-belt set absorbed by kana stations 1–3 (greetings, aizuchi, numbers 1–10, 私/あなた/人/先生/友達, はい/いいえ) — choose words commonly written in kana or displayable in kana. AVOID: time/calendar words, verbs, adjectives, food, places, home objects (other files). Ids v-n5-0001…v-n5-0135 in corpus order; the station assigner gives these items to Stations 1–4, so put the most frequent/concrete words first. Exactly 1 example sentence per word (≤ 25 chars, polite register), using only vocabulary/grammar at N5 or easier. Pass 1 runs every file in parallel with NO known-set snapshot: your packet carries `docs/vocab-ownership.json` (word → owning file, generated from these briefs and linted for double-claims, self-contradictions and dangling skips before packets go out); do not add a word it assigns elsewhere. Cross-file duplicates that slip through are resolved at merge time (lowest level keeps the row; same level → lower file number keeps it; the other row is dropped and its id left as a gap). "skip" in the lists above marks words owned by another file or level — do not include them. Pitch: fill `pitch` (nucleus mora, 0 = heiban) for every word and ALWAYS set `pitchConfidence: "low"` — never "high" (V18 warns); a post-pass sets "high" only where a licensed pitch dataset agrees.
